sentences.text: Once you’ve decided there’s a risk, Rule eight tells you how to act.
Your action should be positive, made in ample time, and with good seamanship.
It should be big enough to be obvious, whether the other captain is watching with his eyes or on radar.
A five degree nudge is invisible.
A forty degree turn tells a story.
Which is why the rule says to avoid a series of small alterations.
And if you have sea room, a course change alone is often your best move, as long as it’s early, substantial, and doesn’t just set you up for another close call with someone else.
Think of it like driving: signal clearly, commit, and don’t weave.
